label: Focus legend
summary: Makes the legends window focus on the given legend.
details: Vanilla calls it when a legend item in the window is clicked or right-clicked, passing that item's own legend. It returns nothing.

label: Legitimacy level itself
summary: The legitimacy level itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more and vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Level number
summary: The position of the legitimacy level in the list of levels, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as the current level next to the highest one, as "level/highest", where the highest is the number of levels minus one.

label: Level effects text
summary: The text describing the effects of the legitimacy level.
details: Vanilla puts it below an "Effects:" heading in the text about what a legitimacy level does.

label: Level entered text
summary: The text describing what happens when a character enters the legitimacy level.
details: Vanilla uses it in the texts of the effect that changes legitimacy ("You increase your legitimacy level to ..."), and only adds it when it is not empty. It takes one argument; the input does not show which one, so the description of the argument is a guess from the name.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; probably the character it is about.

label: Level threshold
summary: How much legitimacy a given character needs to reach this level.
details: Vanilla shows it in the legitimacy track tooltip as "Requires at least X legitimacy", passing the character. The number can have decimals.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the threshold is worked out for.

label: Legitimacy level
summary: The legitimacy level itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the legitimacy type's flavor name function to get the name of the level.

label: Legitimacy type itself
summary: The legitimacy type itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more and vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Flat icon
summary: The flat (plain) icon picture of the legitimacy type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image in the main HUD.

label: Flavor name of level
summary: The themed name of a legitimacy level for this legitimacy type.
details: Vanilla gives it a level and shows the result, for example in the average expectations tooltip, where it lists the level for powerful vassals and for vassals.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the legitimacy type.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' GetIcon is used as an image texture, this is a picture. The game has no direct use of it on this type.

label: Type number
summary: The position of the legitimacy type in the list of types, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and its return type. The input has no direct use of it on this type.

label: Key
summary: The script key of the legitimacy type, as text.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' GetKey is used (for example a building's key in debug texts). The input has no direct use of it on this type.

label: Level name
summary: The name of a legitimacy level of this type.
details: Going by its name and its argument. The same name on the house aspiration type is used to get the name of a level by its number; for this type the input has no use, so what the argument is stays unclear.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; probably the level or its number.

label: Levels
summary: The list of legitimacy levels of this type.
details: Vanilla counts its entries to find the highest level, and it is used in the average expectations tooltip.

label: Levels icon
summary: The picture showing the levels of the legitimacy type.
details: Vanilla uses it, reached through the character's legitimacy type, as the texture of an image in the HUD, the character window and the ledger.

label: Maximum legitimacy
summary: The highest legitimacy value a given character can have.
details: Vanilla shows it as the upper number in "Legitimacy current/maximum" and uses it as the maximum of a bar in the ledger. The number can have decimals.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the maximum is worked out for.

label: Name
summary: The name of the legitimacy type.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tooltip heading "legitimacy level for a ...".

label: Text icon
summary: The small icon of the legitimacy type, written as part of a text.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' GetTextIcon is used inside texts. The input has no direct use of it on this type.

label: Has flat icon
summary: Whether the legitimacy type has a flat icon.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the legitimacy type has an icon.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' HasIcon is used to show an icon only when there is one. The input has no direct use on this type.

label: Has levels icon
summary: Whether the legitimacy type has a levels icon.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the legitimacy type is valid.
details: Vanilla combines it with a check that the character's government has the legitimacy rule, to show legitimacy parts of the HUD and the dynastic cycle window only then. The input does not say exactly what makes a type valid.

label: Localize
summary: Looks up the text for a localization key.
details: Going by its name and the global Localize function, which vanilla uses to turn a built key into a text. The input has no direct use of it on this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The localization key to look up.

label: Legitimacy type
summary: The legitimacy type itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Levy view itself
summary: The levy view itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Close
summary: Closes the levy window.
details: Vanilla runs it when the close button of the levy window is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Levy type
summary: The type of levy the view shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the levy window, so the window's parts read from it.

label: Living levy count
summary: The number of living members of the levy, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it as the first number in "living/maximum" in the levy window.

label: Levy upkeep
summary: The gold cost per month of keeping the levy.
details: Vanilla shows it as "Maintenance: gold/month" with two decimals.

label: Maximum levy count
summary: The most levy men there can be.
details: Vanilla shows it as the second number in "alive/maximum" in the levy window.

label: Raised levy count
summary: How many levy men are raised (called up).
details: Vanilla shows it in the text "X raised".

label: Has raised levies
summary: Whether any levies are raised.
details: Vanilla uses it to show one part of the levy window when levies are raised and another when not.

label: Levy view
summary: The levy view itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Lifestyle itself
summary: The lifestyle itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Background
summary: The background picture of the lifestyle.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of an image in the lifestyle window.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the lifestyle.
details: Vanilla shows it in the lifestyle window and in the tooltip for selecting a lifestyle.

label: Highlight description
summary: The highlight description text of the lifestyle.
details: Vanilla shows it in a weaker style below the description in the lifestyle window. Going by its name, it belongs to the highlight state of the lifestyle.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the lifestyle.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of images in the lifestyle window.

label: Lifestyle number
summary: The position of the lifestyle in the list of lifestyles, as a whole number.
details: Going by its name and its return type. The input has no direct use of it on this type.

label: Key
summary: The script key of the lifestyle, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it to build the name of a sound event when a lifestyle is clicked, and to compare with the key of the selected lifestyle.

label: Name
summary: The name of a lifestyle, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as 'Has the … lifestyle' and 'You can unlock a new Perk for the … Lifestyle'.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the lifestyle, without a tooltip on hover.
details: Vanilla uses it in the lifestyle window texts, for example in tooltip headings and the experience text.

label: Perks in lifestyle
summary: How many perks the lifestyle has.
details: Vanilla shows it as the total in "perks unlocked/total".

label: Experience per level
summary: How much experience a lifestyle level needs.
details: Vanilla shows it as the second number in the experience tooltip "current/needed" and as the maximum of the experience bar.

label: Has background
summary: Whether the lifestyle has a background picture.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the lifestyle has an icon.
details: Going by its name and the way other types' HasIcon is used to show an icon only when there is one. The input has no direct use on this type.

label: Is highlighted
summary: Whether the lifestyle is highlighted for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the highlight marks in the lifestyle window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the highlight is checked for.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the lifestyle is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show or hide parts of the lifestyle window and to set a part as not reacting to the mouse (alwaystransparent). The input does not say exactly what makes a lifestyle valid.

label: Localize
summary: Looks up the text for a localization key.
details: Going by its name and the global Localize function, which vanilla uses to turn a built key into a text. The input has no direct use of it on this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The localization key to look up.

label: Lifestyle
summary: The lifestyle itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to character functions, for example to get a character's perk points or experience in that lifestyle.

label: Light itself
summary: The court scene light itself, in the form needed to change it.
details: Vanilla passes it to the court scene editor's handlers when a light's description is edited, its colour changes or its type is selected. So it is used where the editor changes the light.

label: Light
summary: The court scene light itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the court scene editor to expand or collapse a light, check if it is expanded and read its description.

label: Succession item itself
summary: The line of succession entry itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Character
summary: The character at this place in the line of succession.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the realm window, so the entry's parts read from that character.

label: Succession order
summary: The place of the entry in the line of succession, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it in bold before the character's name in the realm window.

label: Trait lists
summary: The trait lists of the entry's character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the realm window. The return type is a trait arrays object; the input does not say how the traits are grouped.

label: Succession item
summary: The line of succession entry itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Load window itself
summary: The in-game load window itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Save games
summary: The list of saved games the load window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the list in the load screen.

label: Selected save game
summary: The saved game that is selected in the load window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the detail part of the load screen.

label: Has selected save game
summary: Whether a saved game is selected in the load window.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show one part of the load screen when something is selected and another when not.

label: Go back
summary: Leaves the load window and goes back.
details: Vanilla runs it when two controls of the load screen are clicked. Going by its name it goes back. It returns nothing.

label: Delete save game
summary: Deletes the selected saved game.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the load screen. Going by its name it acts on the selected save; the input does not say whether the game asks first.

label: Delete all save games
summary: Deletes all saved games.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button in the load screen. Going by its name it affects every save; the input does not say which ones count or whether the game asks first.

label: Load save game
summary: Loads the selected saved game.
details: Vanilla runs it when a control in the load screen is clicked. Going by its name it loads the selected save. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle invalid saves
summary: Switches whether invalid saved games are shown in the list.
details: Vanilla runs it when a control in the load screen is clicked. Going by the matching ShouldShowInvalidSavegames, the state it switches is the one shown as checked.

label: Load window
summary: The in-game load window itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Shows invalid saves
summary: Whether the load window currently shows invalid saved games.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the checkbox that toggles this.

label: Lobby helper itself
summary: The lobby helper window itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Has government
summary: Whether the given character has a government, as the game's lobby helper sees it.
details: It takes one character. Vanilla uses it in the map icons: a landless ruler's domicile gets a pin on the map only when its type has a lobby map pin and this is yes. Which government is meant is not shown.

label: Close
summary: Closes the lobby helper window.
details: Going by its name and the way other windows' Close is used on close buttons. The input has no direct use on this type.

label: Filtered domicile count
summary: How many domiciles in the given province pass the lobby's current filter.
details: Vanilla uses it on the map: it shows a "+N more" marker (the count minus one) when more than one domicile is there.

label: Character list
summary: The character list part of the multiplayer lobby, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the multiplayer lobby window.

label: DLC collection
summary: The collection of DLCs the lobby shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context in the multiplayer lobby. The input does not say which DLCs are in it.

label: First valid domicile
summary: The position of the first domicile in the province that passes the lobby's filter.
details: Vanilla uses it on the map as an index, and to skip entries of the province's domicile list: it skips this index plus one, so the first valid domicile is skipped too.

label: Landless government filters
summary: The list of government filters for landless rulers in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the filter selection in the multiplayer lobby.

label: Selected government filter
summary: The position of the chosen landless government filter.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the filter list. The return type is a pair of whole numbers, and the input does not say what the two numbers stand for.

label: Selected landless government
summary: The landless government chosen in the lobby.
details: Going by its name. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Landless designing text
summary: The text about starting to design a landless ruler of the given kind for the character, going by its name.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the multiplayer window, passing the character and a kind such as noble_family or landless_adventurer.

label: Landless tab selected
summary: Whether the landless tab is selected in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it on the map to choose which kind of domicile markers to show.

label: Government filter chosen
summary: Applies the government filter the player just chose.
details: Vanilla runs it when the selection in the filter list changes.

label: Lobby helper
summary: The lobby helper window itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Select landless tab
summary: Sets whether the landless tab is selected in the lobby.
details: Vanilla runs it when parts of the lobby start, with no or yes.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Whether the landless tab is selected.

label: Player itself
summary: The lobby player itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can remove player
summary: Whether the player can be removed from the lobby by the viewer.
details: Vanilla uses it to show and enable the remove button.

label: Player ID
summary: The number identifying the lobby player.
details: Vanilla passes it to a check of whether that player is designing a ruler, to choose the text "Ruler designing" or "Not ready".

label: Loading text
summary: A text about the player's loading state.
details: Going by its name. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Lobby view
summary: The lobby view the player belongs to.
details: Going by its name and its return type. The game documents nothing more and vanilla does not use it.

label: Player name
summary: The name of the lobby player.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the lobby's player list.

label: Playable
summary: The playable (ruler) this player controls.
details: Vanilla reaches the player's character through it, to use as the data context and to show the character's name.

label: Transfer progress
summary: How far the player's joining (data transfer) has come, going by its name.
details: Vanilla shows it with a percent format in "Joining... X%".

label: Has playable
summary: Whether the player controls a playable (ruler).
details: Vanilla combines it with the observer and hotjoining checks to decide which parts of the lobby to show.

label: Is host
summary: Whether the player is the host of the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a host mark in the player list.

label: Is hotjoining
summary: Whether the player is joining a game already in progress.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a joining state and to leave out the playable parts then. The meaning of hotjoining comes from the name and these uses.

label: Is local player
summary: Whether the player is the one sitting at this computer.
details: Vanilla uses it to show parts only for yourself or only for others.

label: Is observer
summary: Whether the player only watches the game and plays no ruler.
details: Vanilla uses it to show an observer mark and to leave out the ruler parts for observers.

label: Is ready
summary: Whether the player has marked themselves as ready.
details: Vanilla shows the ready mark only when this is true and the player is not an observer.

label: Remove player
summary: Removes the player from the lobby.
details: Vanilla runs it on the remove button of a player, which is only shown when CanRemovePlayer is true.

label: Player
summary: The lobby player itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Show ready status
summary: Whether the player's ready status should be shown.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Local player
summary: The lobby player of the person at this computer.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the part showing your own player.

label: Selected playable (access)
summary: The playable (ruler) selected in the lobby, in the form needed to change it.
details: Going by its name and the other Access functions. The game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Lobby view itself
summary: The lobby view itself, in the form the game uses when something is passed on for use.
details: Going by its name and the other AccessSelf functions, it hands over the object it is called on. The game documents nothing more.

label: Can control
summary: Whether the viewer can take control of the given playable (ruler).
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the button for choosing a character, and in the other part also requires the character to be a ruler.

label: Can go back
summary: Whether the viewer can leave the lobby and go back.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the back button.

label: Can ready
summary: Whether the viewer can mark themselves as ready.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Can start
summary: Whether the game can be started from the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it to enable the start button.

label: Can start ruler designing
summary: Whether the ruler designer can be started for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it to show and enable a control in the multiplayer window, together with a check that the designer is offered at all.

label: Clear selection
summary: Clears the current selection in the lobby.
details: Vanilla runs it when a control in the multiplayer window is clicked.

label: Take control
summary: Makes the viewer's player control the given playable (ruler).
details: Vanilla runs it when a character is clicked in the lobby.

label: Copy server ID
summary: Copies the ID of the server to the clipboard.
details: Vanilla runs it on a button in the lobby. Going by its name; the input does not say where the copy goes.

label: Control tooltip
summary: The tooltip text for taking control of the given playable.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of controls that take a character, in both multiplayer windows. Going by its name it is the tooltip for taking control.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The playable the tooltip is about.

label: Enabled DLCs
summary: The list of DLCs enabled in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list and checks if it is empty.

label: Enabled mods
summary: The list of mods enabled in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list and checks if it is empty.

label: Go back tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the back button in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it as that button's tooltip.

label: Open multiplayer tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the button that opens the game to multiplayer.
details: Vanilla builds the tooltip of that button from it and adds an achievements note when needed.

label: Other players count
summary: How many players there are besides the viewer.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Ready tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the ready button.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Select button text
summary: The text of the main button in the multiplayer lobby.
details: Vanilla shows it on the button that takes control of the selected character and marks the player ready; that button's tooltip is GetControlToolTip.

label: Selected playable
summary: The playable (ruler) currently selected in the lobby.
details: Vanilla reaches the selected character through it, for example for the capital's name in the ruler designer.

label: Selection click index
summary: A whole number counting the selection clicks in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of a widget in the lobby. The input does not say more about what it counts.

label: Server info
summary: The information about the server of the lobby.
details: Vanilla reads from it whether the lobby is an invite and the server's name.

label: Transfer speed setting
summary: The position of the chosen data transfer speed setting.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the speed option list.

label: Transfer speed options
summary: The list of data transfer speed settings to choose from.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the speed option list.

label: Ruler designing text
summary: The text telling whether the ruler designer can be started for the given character.
details: Vanilla uses it as the tooltip of the design button.

label: Go back
summary: Leaves the lobby and goes back.
details: Vanilla runs it when a control in the multiplayer window is clicked. Going by its name it goes back. CanGoBack is used for an enabled state in the same file.

label: Has enabled DLCs
summary: Whether the multiplayer lobby has any enabled DLCs to list.
details: Vanilla enables the buttons that open and close the lobby's list of enabled DLCs only when this is yes.

label: Has enabled mods
summary: Whether the multiplayer lobby has any enabled mods to list.
details: Vanilla enables the buttons that open and close the lobby's list of enabled mods only when this is yes.

label: Has game configuration window
summary: Whether the lobby has a game configuration window.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Has selected playable
summary: Whether a playable (ruler) is selected in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the character details only when something is selected, and in an enabled check together with a check on the character.

label: Has server info
summary: Whether the lobby has information about its server.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the player and settings parts only when there is server info.

label: Is auto accept
summary: Whether the lobby's auto accept option is on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a checkbox. What exactly is accepted comes only from the name.

label: Is invite only
summary: Whether the lobby is joined by invitation.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show different parts of the lobby settings.

label: Is observer
summary: Whether the viewer is only observing the game.
details: Vanilla uses it to switch the observe button's text between "disable observe" and "observe" and to show parts only for players.

label: Is public with crossplay
summary: Whether the lobby is public and open to crossplay.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show the matching option state in the lobby settings. Going by the name, crossplay means players on other platforms.

label: Is public without crossplay
summary: Whether the lobby is public but closed to crossplay.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show the matching option state in the lobby settings. Going by the name, crossplay means players on other platforms.

label: Is ready
summary: Whether the viewer has marked themselves as ready.
details: Vanilla uses it, together with a check that the viewer is not the host, to show the ready state.

label: Name edited
summary: Handles the lobby name text being edited.
details: Vanilla runs it each time the name field's text changes. It returns nothing.

label: Password edited
summary: Handles the lobby password text being edited.
details: Vanilla runs it each time the password field's text changes. It returns nothing.

label: Transfer speed changed
summary: Applies the transfer speed setting the player just chose.
details: Vanilla runs it when the selection in the speed option list changes.

label: Open game configuration
summary: Opens the game configuration window of the lobby.
details: Going by its name; the game documents nothing more and does not use it.

label: Open multiplayer
summary: Opens the game to multiplayer.
details: Vanilla runs it when a control in the multiplayer window is clicked. Going by its name it opens the game to multiplayer.

label: Players
summary: The list of players in the lobby.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the player list and counts it to show a part when fewer than two are there.

label: Ready
summary: Marks the viewer as ready.
details: Vanilla runs it on the ready button of the lobby.

label: Lobby view
summary: The lobby view itself, to pass on to other functions.
details: The input has no use of it on this type. The same name is used in the game's texts on other types in the same way.

label: Set invite only
summary: Makes the lobby invite only.
details: Vanilla runs it on a button in the lobby settings. Going by its name and the IsInvite check next to it.

label: Set lobby name
summary: Applies the name typed for the lobby.
details: Vanilla runs it when return is pressed in the name field and on a button next to it.

label: Set lobby password
summary: Applies the password typed for the lobby.
details: Vanilla runs it when return is pressed in the password field and on a button next to it.

label: Set public with crossplay
summary: Makes the lobby public and open to crossplay.
details: Vanilla runs it on a button in the lobby settings. Going by its name and the IsPublicCrossplay check next to it.
